cues.say: Component 11: Cache with a short TTL. A small, very fast memory (Redis) holding recent answers. The TTL is how long a copy lives before it's fetched again. You'll bring this up during the spike defenses.
Think of it as: A sticky note with today's specials, rewritten every 2 seconds. Use it for slots left, menu, and catalog.
Here's a real scenario. Game day: 20,000 people refresh slots left, about 500 requests a second.
Without it: 500 identical database queries every second.
With it: First request every 2 seconds reads the database and saves to Redis.
Everyone else gets the Redis copy in under 1 milliseconds.
Stale 3 left? Checkout's conditional update says sold out.
Why it works: 2-second-old numbers are fine for browsing; the sale is still decided by the database.
In the interview, say: Cached for 2 seconds. It's a hint; the database is the truth.
A few related terms you may hear.
TTL: Time to live: how long a cached copy is kept.
Invalidation: Deleting copies on every change. Harder than a short TTL.
Stampede: A hot copy expires and thousands hit the database. Let one refresh.
Hot key: One item everyone reads. Also keep a 1 second copy in each server.
